title: Copy to learn, then make it yours
description: Careful copying is one of the oldest ways to learn a craft. The trick is to study while you copy, then step away and create.

body.heading: Copying with your eyes open
paragraphs: Art students have copied master paintings for centuries, and musicians learn favourite songs note by note. Copying slows you down enough to notice decisions you would otherwise miss: why this colour, why this chord, why this sentence works.
Choose something you admire and reproduce it as closely as you can, for practice only. Ask yourself at each step what the maker chose and why.

body.heading: Then close the book
paragraphs: The learning lands in the second step: put the original away and make your own piece using what you noticed. It will come out different, because your hand, your taste and your mistakes are not theirs.
Keep practice copies clearly labelled as studies, and never present them as original work. The honesty matters, and so does the distance between the copy and your own creation.

takeaway: Copy to understand, then close the book and make your own.
